_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: Session handshake performs a real SYNO.API.Auth login (form POST) from config/env credentials, one session file per NAS shared with the fleet device-token cache, bound to the account and the full origin (a sid cached for https:// is never sent to http://), keeping the SynoToken and 2FA trusted-device token; the per-account trusted-device tokens the fleet layer keeps in the same file survive every write; an expired session clears only the rejected sid; a TLS pin over http:// refuses to log in; a refused configuration (address with a user or password, the example placeholder address, a pin over http://) sends nothing; each request carries an atomic sid+SynoToken snapshot
handfixes.why: The generic session_handshake template GETs a static token URL with no credentials; DSM needs an account login, returns sid + synotoken + did, and DSM 7.3.2+ rejects calls without X-SYNO-TOKEN. A regenerated session.go silently sends every request without a session (DSM error 119).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: press support for credential-bearing session logins (form POST with auth_flow_input env vars) in session_handshake

asserts.contains: HTML document (%d bytes; content not shown)

handfixes.summary: HTTP 200 {success:false} becomes an APIError with the DSM error text; relogin once on an expired session; {success:true,data} is unwrapped; a DSM read that comes back without a {success:true,data} envelope is an error
handfixes.why: DSM reports every failure as HTTP 200. Without this a failed call prints the error envelope as if it were data and exits 0 (false green).

asserts.contains: Body: "DSM answered without a data envelope"

handfixes.summary: SYNOLOGY_TLS_FINGERPRINT pins and SYNOLOGY_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY skips TLS verification on the standard transport; no DSM request (probe, login, authenticated read or write, logout) follows a redirect, same origin included: every DSM http.Client's CheckRedirect is dsm.RefuseRedirect, a 3xx net/http returns unfollowed is an error too, the refusal names the status only and is not retried
handfixes.why: Most NAS units serve DSM's self-signed certificate. Only the h2-only browser-chrome transport emits --insecure, and that transport cannot reach DSM over plain HTTP or with HTTP/2 off (DSM's default). DSM's WebAPI never redirects; the generated client followed same-origin redirects on authenticated requests, so a NAS (or anything on the path) answering a read with 302 Location: /webapi/entry.cgi?api=SYNO.ActiveBackup.Task&method=backup&...&_sid=... made the client carry the sid and SynoToken into a backup start through the read-only abb_tasks tool, even with SYNOLOGY_MCP_READ_ONLY=1. TestNoDSMRequestFollowsARedirect, TestMCPReadToolNeverFollowsARedirect and TestEveryHTTPClientRefusesRedirects fail with the generated redirect policy restored.

handfixes.summary: auth login performs the DSM login and caches the session instead of importing browser cookies for the spec's placeholder host; the generated browser-cookie import helpers it replaced (loadSessionCookiesFromFile and three siblings) are deleted, since nothing calls them
handfixes.why: The generated auth login imported cookies for https://nas.example.com:5001 (the spec placeholder), so it could never authenticate a real NAS. The dead helpers were also the only source of three security-gate P1s in auth.go (gosec G304 on the cookie-file read, G124 on two http.Cookie literals); a reprint that restores them restores those findings.

handfixes.summary: Three generated credentials tests that assert access_token precedence are skipped
handfixes.why: Session-handshake auth never reads access_token into AuthHeader; the generated assertions do not apply and fail.

handfixes.summary: abb backup, abb cancel and session logout (DSM write calls are GETs on entry.cgi) answer --dry-run without sending anything, with a preview that names the exact request: the standard {dry_run, action, would} keys (would = the request line, for example GET https://<nas>:5001/webapi/entry.cgi?api=SYNO.ActiveBackup.Task&method=backup&task_ids=%5B5%5D&trigger_type=1&version=1) plus a request object (http_method, nas origin, path, api, api_method, version, params incl. task_ids); the password, sid and SynoToken are never printed
handfixes.why: The generated GET-mutation template wraps the client's dry-run sentinel in the provenance envelope ({meta, results:{dry_run:true}}), which fails the live dogfood dry-run JSON contract (missing top-level dry_run:true) and so the Phase 5 gate. Fix round 1: the preview said only {"would":"run abb backup; no changes made"} (no NAS, DSM call or task ids), so the person approving it saw nothing; dsmDryRun now takes the call site's params and reads the request from the command's own pp:method/pp:path annotations. TestDSMWriteDryRunNamesTheRequest fails with the old preview restored.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: press: give GET-shaped mutations (RPC APIs) the same dry-run short-circuit as POST mutations

return dsmDryRun(cmd, flags, "abb cancel", map[string]string{"task_ids": formatCLIParamValue(flagTaskIds)})

handfixes.summary: auth logout forgets, on this computer, the whole cached session file of the NAS SYNOLOGY_BASE_URL (or the config's base_url, or --nas <registered name>) names - every account's sid, SynoToken, cookies and two-factor trusted-device tokens - or with --all every session file the CLI wrote, plus the login stored in the CLI's own config (credential fields of config.json, the credentials file); it removes only files it can prove it wrote (the name is exactly the CLI's scheme - session-<scheme>-<host>_<port>[_<path>]-<hash8>.json in the data directory, the legacy session.json, or either's .<name>.<digits>.tmp - AND the content parses as the record the CLI writes under that name, a per-NAS record's origin naming the file), never follows a symbolic link, and lists every other session-cache-like file as skipped (kept); it prints every file it removed, changed or kept (or 'nothing cached for <address>'), never contacts the NAS and says so, keeps --dry-run truthful with the same JSON shape as the run (every list [] when empty, never null), and with no usable NAS address refuses (exit 2, naming SYNOLOGY_BASE_URL, --nas and --all) instead of reporting 'cleared' for the example placeholder
handfixes.why: The generated logout cleared only what the current shell named: in a fresh shell (SYNOLOGY_BASE_URL unset) it targeted https://nas.example.com:5001, cleared nothing, wrote a config.json naming the placeholder and still printed {"cleared": true} / 'Logged out. Credentials cleared.', so the next command reused the live sid with no password; with SYNOLOGY_BASE_URL set and SYNOLOGY_ACCOUNT unset it removed the sid but kept the account's trusted-device token, so the next password login skipped the second factor. TestAuthLogoutInAFreshShell, TestAuthLogoutWithoutAnAccount and TestAuthLogoutForgetsOnlyTheNamedNAS (against a two-factor DSM stand-in: after logout the next command needs the password and a one-time code) fail with the contract reverted. Round 5: --all deleted every file NAMED like a session cache in the config directory (--config, SYNOLOGY_CONFIG, SYNOLOGY_CONFIG_DIR can point at a shared or per-client folder), so a user's session.json, session-planning-2026.json and .session-keep.tmp were removed; and the dry-run printed session_files null where the run printed []. TestSessionCacheFilesAreProvenBeforeRemoval, TestAuthLogoutKeepsFilesItDidNotWrite and TestAuthLogoutPreviewAndRunHaveOneShape fail with the proof, the data-directory scoping or the list normalisation reverted.

handfixes.summary: --csv, --plain and --quiet output drops terminal control characters (C0 except tab/CR/LF, DEL, C1) from NAS-sourced values
handfixes.why: Task, host and share names come from the NAS, and the generated printCSV/printPlain/printQuiet/quietScalar wrote them raw, so a name carrying ESC ] 52 ; c ; ... BEL (OSC 52, the clipboard) or ESC [ 2 J reached the terminal. Measured on the shipped tree against a stub NAS: `abb tasks --csv`, `--plain` and `group list --quiet` printed raw ESC, BEL and U+009D. Ported from bitdefender/backup-radar (same press 4.33.5 template). The hand-written fleet and abb report tables already go through printAutoTable/formatCellValue, which scrub. TestTabularPrintersScrubTerminalControls fails with the scrub removed.

handfixes.summary: every terminal write in every package goes through the shared escaping writers in internal/termio (stdoutW()/stderrW() in internal/cli, termio.Stderr() in client, store, config, cliutil, learn, platform and the MCP main): UTF-8 C1, lone 8-bit C1, raw C0/DEL (except tab, newline, CR before newline) become \u00XX; only the CLI's own SGR colors pass; isTerminal unwraps the writer; sync progress redraws through termio.Progress
handfixes.why: encoding/json escapes C0 but writes U+0080-U+009F raw, and xterm/VTE act on UTF-8 C1 (CSI, OSC, ST): `abb tasks --json` against a stub NAS printed a task name's U+009D...U+009C raw; and 150 generated fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, ...) sites (dry-run request bodies, retry notes, warnings) bypassed any writer. Ported from backup-radar (termio converged there over 4 Codex rounds). TestExecuteEscapesControlsOnStdoutAndStderr runs the real Execute() and fails with the SetOut/SetErr wiring removed; TestNoDirectTerminalWrites walks the module and fails on any new direct stream write; TestIsTerminalUnwrapsEscapingWriter pins the unwrap.

handfixes.summary: every MCP tool result and error text (typed endpoint tools, the why_did_a_task_fail intent and the Cobra-mirror tools) is built through an escaping constructor (mcpResultText/mcpResultError, escapedToolResultText/Error/escapedTextContent) that rewrites C0, DEL and C1 controls as \u00XX
handfixes.why: The typed endpoint tools returned DSM JSON verbatim and mcp-go encodes the frame with encoding/json, so a task name carrying U+009D...U+009C (OSC 52) reached content[].text and the stdio frame raw; measured on the shipped binary: abb_tasks and why_did_a_task_fail answered with raw C1 on the wire. Ported from backup-radar. TestEndpointResultEscapesTaskName (fake NAS) fails with the escape removed; TestToolHandlersUseEscapingConstructors fails if any handler calls mcplib.NewToolResultText/Error or NewTextContent directly.

asserts.contains: func escapeTerminalControls(s string) string { return termio.EscapeString(s) }

handfixes.summary: when a shelled-out command exits non-zero with output on both streams, the MCP error result carries its stdout as well as stderr, so fleet status, fleet health and the abb reports (exit 6 with findings) hand an agent the rows, not only the count
handfixes.why: The report commands exit 6 exactly when they found something; RunCLICommand quoted stderr alone, so the abb_failures MCP tool answered `Error: 1 row(s) need attention` with the rows dropped (measured on the shipped binary against a stub NAS). Same shape as quotewerks mcp-partial-failure-keeps-receipt. TestShellOutFindingsKeepRows (a helper process that prints rows and exits 6) fails without the branch.

handfixes.summary: the MCP context tool, the search/sql tool descriptions and the sql no-such-table hint describe DSM truthfully: GET operations selected by api=/method=, offset/limit paging with the real defaults, the fleet mirror filled by fleet_sync, sql/search covering only the generic sync store (folder, group, package, user; the DSM system log is read live with log_list and is neither syncable nor searchable), registry administration (fleet add/remove) named as CLI-only and tail as not an MCP tool, archetype infrastructure, no developer-platform playbook, real auth env descriptions
handfixes.why: The generated context tool (`call this first`) told agents lists page with a cursor (default 100), marked abb, storage and system searchable although sync never stores them, pointed the sql tool and its no-such-table hint at resource_type='abb' rows that never exist, described SYNOLOGY_PASSWORD/DEVICE_ID/OTP_CODE as `Set during initial auth setup.` and shipped a developer-platform archetype and playbook. Same class bitdefender and backup-radar fixed. TestMCPContextDescribesDSM fails with the old archetype or the cursor tip restored.

handfixes.summary: the fleet and abb reports (fleet sync/status/health/list, abb failures/stale/device/trend via printFleetRows, and abb triage) keep every field their row types declare under --agent/--compact (printReportJSON: printJSONFilteredKeep with the reflected JSON field names)
handfixes.why: --agent compaction keeps a row key only when it is on the gravity allow-list or present on 80% of rows, and the report rows mark their reconciliation fields omitempty. Measured on the shipped binary with five registered NAS units, one unreachable: `fleet sync --agent` printed n5 as ok:false with its error dropped and `fleet status --agent` dropped sync_error; abb triage lost error_code and params on the failing timeline step. TestAgentCompactionKeepsReportFields fails with the keep set removed.

handfixes.summary: ApplyProfileToFlags marks every flag it applies as Changed, so a profile value behaves like a typed one
handfixes.why: Commands gate on Changed(): abb backup/cancel run their required-input check and --task-ids JSON validation only when the flag changed, hasChangedLocalFlags decides whether a bare call prints help, --agent fills json/compact/no-input only where they are unchanged. A profile value applied without Changed was ignored (help printed, nothing ran) or sent unvalidated. The backup-radar safety case (a saved --dry-run running live) is not reachable here because the DSM write commands read flags.dryRun directly, but the class is the same template code. TestApplyProfileMarksFlagsChanged fails without the line.

handfixes.summary: a typed output-mode flag (json/csv/plain/quiet/agent) or projection (compact/select) wins over every profile value in its group
handfixes.why: ApplyProfileToFlags overlaid by flag name only, so a typed --csv or --plain lost to a profile's --json: measured on the shipped binary, `profile save pj --json` then `group list --profile pj --csv` printed JSON. TestApplyProfileTypedOutputModeWins fails without the group rule.

handfixes.summary: the typed MCP write tools (abb_backup, abb_cancel, session_logout) refuse any argument outside their schema, and every typed read tool refuses an argument that would override its fixed DSM query (api, method, version, _sid, SynoToken, or any key its path fixes), before any request
handfixes.why: makeAPIHandler forwarded undeclared arguments as query parameters and the client merges them into the path's own query with Set. Every DSM operation is a GET on one CGI path selected by api=/method=, so with SYNOLOGY_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 the read-only abb_tasks tool called with {"method":"backup"} started a backup and abb_settings with {"api":"SYNO.ActiveBackup.Task","method":"cancel"} cancelled one, and abb_backup with the CLI spelling dry-run:true ran live (all three measured on the shipped binary against a stub NAS). TestEndpointWriteRefusesUndeclaredArgument and TestReadToolRefusesOperationOverride fail with the check removed and prove declared calls and a harmless extra filter still reach the NAS.

Measured on the shipped binary with SYNOLOGY_MCP_READ_ONLY=1: tools/list still offered abb_backup, abb_cancel, session_logout and six local writers, and tools/call sent backup, cancel and logout to a stub NAS. Same defect td-synnex and quotewerks fixed. TestReadOnlyEnvDropsEndpointWrites fails without the call (and on any offered tool lacking readOnlyHint); TestReadOnlyCallTimeBackstop fails without the backstop.

Same fix as td-synnex mcp-read-only-fails-closed. TestReadOnlyEnvDropsEndpointWrites (values 1/true/yes) fails with the literal-1 check restored. Codex round 6: a literal ${READ_ONLY} value was read as unset through EnvOverride and left the write tools in place; only the switch's own unfilled MCPB placeholder now reads as unset.

handfixes.summary: the sync --full / --latest-only and workflow archive cursor clears mark a collection incomplete (store.ClearSyncCursor), run only after every flag is validated, and only for known resource names; the hand-written fleet mirror commits data and outcome together after the walk and has no pre-walk clear
handfixes.why: The generated clears wrote last_attempt_complete=1 for every collection before validating --since or walking anything: measured on the shipped tree, `sync --full --since bogus` exited with a usage error and left five sync_state rows marked complete with zero rows, so MCP search/sql reported store_status ready (false-GREEN). Ported from backup-radar. TestClearSyncCursorNeverMarksComplete fails with complete=1; TestSyncUsageErrorsLeaveSyncStateUntouched fails with the clear moved back before validation.

Ported from backup-radar. TestDryRunChangesNothingLocally fails with any of the three guards removed.

handfixes.summary: auth setup and the unauthenticated auth status print the DSM login setup for macOS/Linux and PowerShell; auth status treats SYNOLOGY_ACCOUNT plus SYNOLOGY_PASSWORD (or an auth_header session id) as configured and names what is missing
handfixes.why: auth setup printed `No setup URL is configured for this CLI; check the API's docs.` and named no variable, and auth status read only auth_header: measured on the shipped binary with the account and password set, even right after a successful auth login, it printed `Not authenticated`, a bare `Set your token:` and exited 4. Most MSPs run PowerShell, where `export` does not exist. TestAuthSetupPrintsBothShells and TestAuthStatusReadsDSMLogin fail with the generated text restored.

handfixes.summary: every user-facing POSIX-only form carries its PowerShell twin: the auth login `SYNOLOGY_OTP_CODE=... cmd` example, the fleet sync `credentials not set` hint, and the mcp-install remote launch line
handfixes.why: PowerShell has no `VAR=value cmd` prefix and rejects `<`; the fleet sync row error said `export <prefix>_ACCOUNT and <prefix>_PASSWORD` only, and mcp-install.md gave only the POSIX launch line. The PowerShell launch line keeps `VAR=` with no spaces so check_env_schema still sees each required variable. TestHelpExamplesCarryPowerShellTwin and TestFleetSyncCredentialHintCarriesPowerShellTwin fail with the twins removed.

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's --transport http bearer token, SYNOLOGY_TLS_FINGERPRINT and SYNOLOGY_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY are read through cliutil.EnvOverride, so an unresolved ${user_config...} placeholder reads as unset (no bearer secret, no certificate pin) instead of as a value

Same fix as sophos-central, bitdefender and backup-radar. TestHTTPTokenPlaceholderRefused and TestEnvTLSIgnoresUnresolvedPlaceholders fail with os.Getenv restored.

The copy-paste blocks also set optional variables to `<your-...>` text, which a pasted config would send as a one-time code, a device token, a certificate pin, an HTTP token and (now that the switch fails closed) read-only mode. handfixes.summary: no credential-named field (password, passwd, secret, token, private key, API key, sid, did, ...) from a DSM answer reaches disk: rows are redacted at the single store sink (upsertGenericResourceTx, which sync, write-through live reads and the FTS index share), and an answer carrying one is never written to the HTTP response cache; live output is unchanged
handfixes.why: The spec declares no response schemas, so the secret-bearing reads cannot be enumerated; the class is reachable mechanically. Measured on the shipped binary against a stub NAS serving SENTINEL-SECRET-7731 in user passwd, share enc_passwd, Hyper Backup repo_password, ABB smtp_password and network pppoe_password: `sync` and the write-through of `hyperbackup tasks` stored it in data.db (which MCP sql serves even in read-only mode) and the response cache kept three copies. The fleet mirror stores typed columns only (first_error uses an allow-list of log params), so fleet sync never stored it. No synology GET is known or declared to return credential material, so no command moved to the Credential tier. TestSyncAndLiveReadsNeverPersistSecretFields walks the whole home after sync and live reads and fails with either sink's redaction removed; TestStoreNeverPersistsSecretFields and TestResponseCacheNeverStoresSecretFields pin each sink.

handfixes.summary: fleet add, fleet remove (registry administration) and tail are never MCP tools (mcp:hidden), in full and read-only mode; fleet_sync stays exposed and reaches only operator-registered NAS units
handfixes.why: fleet_add took url and env-prefix from the agent, so {url: attacker, env-prefix: SYNOLOGY, check: true} (or a later fleet_sync) POSTed SYNOLOGY_PASSWORD, or any <prefix>_PASSWORD in the server's env, to a host the agent chose; fleet_remove let an agent drop a client NAS from monitoring. Measured on the shipped binaries: the attacker host received the password. tail defaults to --follow and polls forever, so an MCP tools/call never returned and hung an unattended agent (no result in 20 s). fleet_add/fleet_remove are hand-written (fleet_registry.go); tail.go is generated. TestMCPOmitsOperatorOnlyAndStreamingTools and TestMCPFleetSyncReachesOnlyRegisteredNAS fail with any of the three annotations removed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: press: an x-mcp-hidden (or streaming) marker for follow/poll commands so tail is never mirrored

handfixes.summary: no flag, --param/--global-param/--resource-param or MCP argument may re-select the DSM operation (api, method, version), the session (_sid, SynoToken) or another key the spec path fixes: dsm.CheckOperationParams runs in the generated client before the dry run and before any login, and in the fleet dsm.Client
handfixes.why: Every DSM operation is a GET on one CGI path selected by api=/method=. handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary

The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).
